name: Mersiline mesh implant
lead: Mersiline mesh is named in a general reference on chin augmentation as one of several alternative implant materials, described there as a mesh scaffold, alongside acellular dermal matrix and braided suture material (Supramid) [1]. The name appears to correspond to Mersilene, a Dacron (polyester) surgical mesh used for decades in hernia repair, prolapse surgery and eyelid-lifting (frontalis suspension) procedures [2][3][4].

Evidence on its use for facial augmentation is very thin. The reviewed medical literature on Mersilene mesh concerns non-cosmetic uses, and a review of alloplastic materials in rhinoplasty is the closest facial-surgery reference [5]. In looksmaxxing it is listed as a hardmaxx implant option for facial contouring, but no cosmetic study of it was found in the material reviewed.
infobox: Hernia repair, vaginal vault prolapse, frontalis suspension for ptosis [2][3][4]

paras: A general chin augmentation reference lists Mersiline among non-standard chin implant materials, describing it as a mesh scaffold [1]. The standard chin options in that reference are silicone, porous polyethylene and ePTFE [1].

Mersilene (Dacron) mesh was described in 1984 as used by two French surgical teams for about 20 years in groin hernia repair [2]. A 1985 report followed 56 patients who underwent abdominal sacral colpopexy for vaginal vault prolapse, in most of whom a synthetic mesh was the interposed material [3]. A 2004 study reported functional results and complications of Mersilene mesh in frontalis suspension for ptosis [4].
A review of alloplastic materials in rhinoplasty appears in Current Opinion in Otolaryngology and Head and Neck Surgery [5]. Its content is not summarised in the sources reviewed beyond its title.

No studies found on Mersiline mesh for facial or chin augmentation in the material reviewed. Related research on Mersilene mesh covers other body regions: hernia repair [2], pelvic prolapse including a registered trial comparing Proline mesh with Mersilene tape (completed, n=80) [6], and eyelid frontalis suspension [4].

card.summary: Polyester mesh named as a facial-augmentation material, but backed by essentially no cosmetic data.
card.note: Cosmetic use is poorly documented; established uses are in hernia, prolapse and eyelid surgery.

quick.overview:
Mersiline is listed as a mesh scaffold among alternative chin implant materials. It seems to refer to Mersilene, a polyester mesh long used in hernia and other surgery.

In looksmaxxing it is a niche hardmaxx implant option; no cosmetic studies were found.
quick.mechanism: A woven synthetic mesh is placed as a scaffold in the tissue. Its established uses are as reinforcement or suspension material elsewhere in the body [2][4].
quick.risks: Cosmetic risks are not documented in the reviewed sources. Studies of Mersilene mesh in other body regions report complications, for example in ptosis surgery [4].
